old_rows.title: Justices Take Up Trump's Asylum Ban. Flights Resume After a Rare Nationwide Halt. A Tanker Hits a River Cruise.
old_rows.description: Justices take up Trump's asylum ban, airlines recover from a rare nationwide ground stop and all survive a New Orleans river crash.

old_rows.title: Microsoft Fights a Global Outage. Trump Threatens Mexico Tariffs. Cisco Posts a Record Quarter.
old_rows.description: Microsoft works to restore Outlook and Teams after a global outage, Trump threatens Mexico tariffs over a caravan, and Cisco posts record sales.

old_rows.title: Food Aid Rules Face a Rewrite. Colom Wins Mississippi. Nvidia Changes Its CEO.
old_rows.description: A SNAP proposal could affect millions, Scott Colom wins Mississippi's Senate race, and Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia.

old_rows.title: Health Data Practices Face a Lawsuit. Claude Expands at Work. Wall Street Rebounds.
old_rows.description: Five states join the Hims & Hers case, Anthropic expands workplace tools, and stocks recover before another Fed decision.

old_rows.title: FDA Adds a Vision Warning to GLP-1 Drugs. A Pill Eases Sleep Apnea. DNA Orders Face Screening.
old_rows.description: The FDA adds a vision loss warning to GLP-1 drugs and Lilly reports sleep apnea results. Plus Anthropic’s IPO and Novaya Gazeta.

old_rows.title: Nvidia Opens a Board Review. Heart Repair Advances in Mice. Climate Talks Begin.
old_rows.description: Nvidia investigates espionage allegations, researchers test heart repair in mice and COP31 opens, plus Egypt’s train collision and AI’s power equipment squeeze.

old_rows.title:
Trump Orders a DOJ Review.
Israel Faces Coalition Talks.
Japan Assesses Quake Damage.
old_rows.description: Trump calls for a review of Democrats, Eisenkot begins coalition bargaining and Japan assesses earthquake damage, plus Poland’s investigation.

old_rows.title: Measles Cases Climb. Stocks Recover Ground. Iran Talks Continue.
old_rows.description: Measles cases exceed 5,000, technology shares regain ground and new U.S. strikes come as Qatar continues Iran mediation.

old_rows.title: Tesla Plans a Factory Shift. Raman Inherits an Olympic Host City. Cash Buyers Skew Older.
old_rows.description: Tesla plans factory changes, Los Angeles chooses a new mayor, and cash buyers reveal a widening gap in access to homes.

old_rows.title: Democrats are projected to take Congress. Tankers burn near Hormuz. Indonesia fires a top aide.
old_rows.description: Democrats are projected to win both chambers of Congress, Iran says four tankers hit mines near Hormuz, and Indonesia's president fires his chief of staff.

old_rows.title: What the Midterms Mean for Your Budget. CVS Plans a Split. Healthcare Stocks Rally.
old_rows.description: The election opens a household-policy debate, CVS plans two companies, and health and energy shares rally.

old_rows.title: America votes today on Congress and 145 ballot measures. Your health insurance is about to cost more. And Netflix wants to read your mood.
old_rows.description: Control of Congress is on the ballot today along with 145 state measures, Obamacare premiums are set to climb, and Netflix starts picking shows by mood.

old_rows.title: Oil lost nearly $9 a barrel in a day. A senator had a stroke at a hockey game. And El Niño is flooding the Southwest.
old_rows.description: Signs that Iran is open to peace talks knocked oil to its steepest one day drop in months, Sen. Chris Murphy had a stroke, and storms drenched the desert Southwest.

old_rows.title: Wall Street had its worst day since June. A judge ended Trump's WSJ lawsuit. And Milwaukee got its parade.
old_rows.description: AI worries sent tech stocks and Intel tumbling, a federal judge ended Trump's case against The Wall Street Journal, and Milwaukee threw its first World Series parade.
